TIP 1: Payroll time edits at Harborline Logistics
CHANNEL: secure drop
RECEIVED: 06 May 2026

I am a senior payroll analyst at Harborline Logistics, working in the Edison, New Jersey distribution hub. This submission concerns overtime-hour adjustments made before weekly payroll runs between 05 January 2026 and 23 March 2026.

The Kronos export showed 1,842 overtime hours for hourly warehouse staff during that period. The final ADP payroll files paid 1,326 overtime hours. Payroll Director Lenora Pike approved manual edits to 74 employee timecards under adjustment code `SUP-MGR-CORR`. The edits removed meal-period overruns and post-shift loading time from the paid total.

I have the Kronos audit report, the ADP import files, and Pike's 12 February 2026 email instructing supervisors to "clear avoidable overtime before payroll close." The estimated underpayment for the quarter is $18,940. I am still employed and request confidential handling.

The edits were not payroll corrections for missed punches. In several examples, the employees had both badge-in and badge-out records, dock assignment logs, and supervisor shift notes confirming they stayed late. The manager correction simply reduced the paid time to the scheduled shift length. The same pattern appears across outbound, returns, and cold-chain loading teams.

I raised the discrepancy to Pike on 28 March 2026 during payroll close. She said operations had already approved the hours and that payroll should "avoid reopening settled weeks." I did not escalate internally after that because my access to the audit export depends on Pike's approval. I can provide a redacted spreadsheet showing employee ID, original punch, adjusted punch, approver, and pay-period impact.

TIP 2: Warehouse overtime was stripped from people who earned it
CHANNEL: intake form
RECEIVED: 07 May 2026

I supervise outbound loading at Harborline Logistics in Edison. I am furious writing this because I watched people work nights away from their kids and then saw the company erase the hours. This is not a misunderstanding. It is shameful.

On 19 February 2026 I watched Operations Manager Caleb Orr tell two leads to change the Kronos punches for the late trailer crew from 11.7 hours to 10.0 hours. The crew had stayed because trailer HLX-4028 arrived late from Elizabeth. Those workers did the work. The next morning their timecards showed a manager correction instead of the actual clock-out time.

I have screenshots from Kronos for employees 4412, 4480, and 4521, plus the dock log showing trailer HLX-4028 arrived at 9:42 PM. People cried in the break room about missing rent money. I cannot sleep knowing I signed off on a shift summary while this happened.

This was not a one-night problem. I saw the same thing after late trailers on 05 February and 12 March. Every time, the explanation from management was that "approved overtime" meant only overtime approved before the shift, even when the delay was caused by Harborline's own dispatch schedule. That is not how we explained overtime to the crew when we asked them to stay.

I am angry because the people affected are the lowest-paid employees in the building, but I am giving you the records that can be checked. The trailer logs, badge swipes, and Kronos correction history all line up. I will speak with an investigator, but I do not want my name given to Orr or Pike while I still supervise the floor.

TIP 3: Wage theft at Harborline as part of an organizing record
CHANNEL: encrypted email
RECEIVED: 08 May 2026

I am a former HR generalist at Harborline Logistics. I am documenting the Edison hub's overtime edits because wage theft is one piece of a broader campaign our worker-justice committee is building against logistics employers that depend on precarious labor.

The underlying records are specific. Between January and March 2026, Payroll Director Lenora Pike and Operations Manager Caleb Orr used Kronos manager corrections to reduce overtime before ADP payroll submission. I reviewed a spreadsheet on 25 March 2026 listing at least 61 affected employees and approximately $16,000 in unpaid overtime.

Our committee intends to use this case to show how private logistics firms externalize labor costs while presenting themselves as efficient. I can provide the March spreadsheet, my exit memo to HR, and the Slack thread where I asked Pike why wage adjustments were being coded as supervisor corrections.

I recognize that my framing is part of a political project. I am not pretending otherwise. The committee has been collecting examples from warehouses, delivery contractors, and temp agencies because we believe wage theft is structural, not accidental. Harborline is useful because the records are unusually clean and show how a respectable company can make underpayment look like routine timekeeping.

The facts should stand apart from my politics. The Kronos correction codes, the ADP payroll totals, and the manager approvals can be tested without accepting my broader view of logistics work. I am including the broader view because it is why I am willing to risk submitting this, not because the records need it to be true.

TIP 4: Harborline executives are stealing from workers
CHANNEL: web form
RECEIVED: 09 May 2026

Harborline Logistics is run by greedy executives who steal from workers because that is what this whole anti-worker system rewards. The people at the top are parasites. They shave hours, deny overtime, and then lecture everyone about efficiency while families suffer.

At the Edison hub, Lenora Pike and Caleb Orr changed Kronos punches in February 2026 before the ADP payroll file went out. They stole hours from dock workers after late trailer shifts. This happened around the week of 19 February 2026 and I know employee 4412 lost overtime.

This is not just one company. It is class warfare dressed up as payroll administration. Harborline, its investors, and every manager who protects them are part of the same machine. Workers should expose them everywhere. I am angry and I hope this burns their reputation down.

There are records if anyone cares enough to look, but Harborline counts on everyone being too tired and scared. Check the Kronos correction history for the Edison hub in February and March 2026. Check who approved the edits. Check how many corrections hit after late trailer nights. They know exactly what they are doing, and they hide behind software codes.

I am not writing politely because politeness is what they demand while taking people's money. This company should be made an example of for every warehouse doing the same thing. If that sounds like an agenda, fine. The agenda is that workers should not be robbed by people in offices who never touch a pallet.
